This is one of the most confusing waiver wires of the season, because most of the names worth a claim depend on injury news that has not settled. Saquon Barkley’s hamstring, Jeremiyah Love’s ankle, Ja’Marr Chase’s concussion and where Tyreek Hill signs all decide how this list plays out, so pay as much attention to the condition next to each name as to the name itself.
If you want these calls made for your exact roster, our Waiver Wire tool gives you recommended waiver wire moves for your specific league.
HIGH ROSTER PERCENTAGE ADDS
Tyler Allgeier  RB · ARI
Probably rostered in your league, but check. Jeremiyah Love hurt his other ankle in Week 4, not the one he sprained before the season, and if Love misses any time, Allgeier is a top 24 back in my rankings in a Cardinals offense that has been far better than the betting markets expected.
Jordyn Tyson  WR · NO
Also likely rostered, and if he is out there, he is worth a big bid. He is still weeks away from returning from his hamstring injury and I would not count on him before the Saints’ Week 8 bye, but he was a top 10 pick in the draft with the talent to be a real weapon in New Orleans once he is healthy.

With Tank Bigsby on injured reserve, Shipley is next in line behind Saquon Barkley
Will Shipley

Shipley is the back I am adding in my own league, and he should be on your waiver wire too. Tank Bigsby has a core muscle injury that needs surgery and went on injured reserve, and Barkley left Week 4 early with a hamstring injury. The early reporting says the hamstring is not serious and he is week to week. But Barkley is an older back who has been banged up all season, so I would not be surprised if Philadelphia rests him for 2 or 3 weeks, and with Bigsby gone, Shipley is the last back standing.
The NFL track record is thin only because he has always been parked behind Barkley, with 30 carries as a rookie, 14 in 2025 and 15 through 4 games this season. He has been the passing down back, especially on third down, and at over 200 pounds, with more than 200 carries in a season at Clemson, he can handle early downs too. I see him as a low end RB2 for as long as Barkley is out, not a top 12 back in an Eagles offense that looks this bad, and if Barkley plays, he is the handcuff you hold.

Wilson took over the Seattle backfield in Week 4, and with Price on injured reserve, the work is his for now. He handled the early downs and still got work as a receiver, which is the profile of a back you can start for as long as the job is his alone.
The window is short, because Charbonnet is working back from the torn ACL he suffered in the playoffs and his practice window opened on Thursday, October 1. Once he is activated, I expect this to turn into a committee. Until then Wilson belongs in your lineup as a flex in a 12 team league, and San Francisco comes to Seattle in Week 5.

Doubs is rostered in more than half of leagues, so he may not be on your wire, but if he is, claim him ahead of the deeper league receivers below. Drake Maye showed signs of life in the win over Buffalo, and with Brown out and Mack Hollins dealing with a calf injury, Doubs is the receiver New England is leaning on.
The catch is the window. New England hopes to have Brown back as soon as Week 6, and once he is healthy, Doubs drops back to a bench receiver you may end up cutting. Until then he is a flex play in a 12 team league, starting with Las Vegas at home in Week 5.

Tyreek Hill

Hill has not played since the knee injury that ended his 2025 season, but his agent says he could sign within days, and he only wants to play for a contender. Kansas City is the obvious fit after Tyquan Thornton dislocated his ankle and Rashee Rice pulled a hamstring, but the Giants and Ravens have been linked to him too, and New England, with AJ Brown on injured reserve, makes sense as well.
Where he lands decides what he is worth, so temper it. His knee injury was severe, and I do not expect him to be the receiver who led the league in yards again, but even a 25% chance he comes close to his old self in a good offense is worth the last spot on your bench.

DEEPER LEAGUES
Khalil Shakir  WR · BUF
Week 4 vs NE: 8 targets · 7 receptions · 82 yards · 13.2 PPR
Led Buffalo in targets in Week 4, the game in which DJ Moore aggravated a shoulder injury. Last season, before Moore got to Buffalo, he averaged 10.4 points per game, so he is a bye week fill in for deeper leagues, and only if Moore is going to miss real time.
Keon Coleman  WR · BUF
Week 4 vs NE: 7 targets · 6 receptions · 116 yards · 23.6 PPR
Had the big game in Week 4, but last season, before Moore got to Buffalo, he averaged under 8 points per game. Like Shakir, he is a desperation flex in deeper leagues and only worth a claim if Moore misses real time.
Roman Wilson  WR · PIT
Week 4 at CLE: 6 targets · 3 receptions · 74 yards · 16.4 PPR
Pittsburgh’s second receiver has drawn 6 targets in every game, including Week 4, when he was knocked out of the game for a stretch. In deeper leagues he is worth a look as a bye week fill in.
Malik Washington  WR · MIA
Week 4 at MIN: 5 targets · 5 receptions · 67 yards · 12.0 PPR
Has at least 5 targets in all 4 games and runs a route on nearly every Malik Willis dropback. Miami projects as one of the worst offenses in the league every week, though, so he is a bye week fill in, not a weekly starter.
Mike Gesicki  TE · CIN
Week 4 vs JAX: 5 targets · 3 receptions · 40 yards · 13.0 PPR
Only a play if Ja’Marr Chase misses Week 5 in the concussion protocol, with Tee Higgins also banged up. Without Chase he can see 5 to 8 targets, and Cincinnati plays Miami before its Week 6 bye.
T.J. Hockenson  TE · MIN
Week 4 vs MIA: 13 targets · 13 receptions · 119 yards · 24.9 PPR
Only a play if Justin Jefferson misses another game with his sprained ankle. With Jefferson out in Week 4, Hockenson caught every pass thrown his way, and Minnesota plays at New Orleans in Week 5.
DON’T CHASE
George Holani  RB · SEA
Week 4 vs LAC: 7 carries · 18 rushing yards · 1 target · 3.0 PPR
I had him under Don’t Chase in Week 2, and Week 4 did not change my mind. Seattle’s backfield belongs to Emanuel Wilson until Zach Charbonnet is back, and Holani did little with the touches he got.
DEFENSES TO STREAM
My pick: Bengals at Dolphins
Miami projects as one of the lowest scoring offenses on the slate, and Cincinnati has a real chance of still being on your waiver wire. It is the best defense you can probably still get.
Also in play
Jets vs Browns · Cowboys vs Buccaneers · Commanders vs Giants
How I pick them
I stream defenses off the betting markets: the biggest spread and the lowest projected total for the other offense. Houston at Tennessee is the best play in Week 5, since the Titans project as the lowest scoring offense in the league, but the Texans are probably rostered.
